clue.text: Spike or peg to put in

indicators.note: put in says the word to goes inside the synonym for peg

parts.note: a peg can be a pin
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for fixing something: insert a spike or a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike a climber hammers into rock.

clue.text: Predicts a conversion — perfect?

indicators.note: a conversion changes the form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rugby fan predicts a conversion will be perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a conversion' suggests rugby; 'conversion' rearranges PREDICTS with A. The question mark marks the adjective as loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled through repetition is expert, close to flawless.

clue.text: Trunk's a third of a ton, approximately

indicators.note: a third of the three-letter word is its first letter

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: A tree trunk weighs roughly a third of a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree; it is the body's trunk. One letter of three is a third of TON.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body without head or limbs, its trunk.

clue.text: Directions an aggressive type gives reporter

parts.note: N, E, W and S are compass directions
a hawk is a warlike person in politics

explanation.surface: A bossy person issues orders to a journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A newshawk is an informal word for a journalist chasing stories.

clue.text: Foreign cricketer, say, bowled all right at end of season

indicators.note: at end of says the bowled and all-right letters follow the season word

parts.note: spring is a season of the year
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A visiting cricketer bowled well late in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: A Springbok is a South African international player, so a touring South African cricketer is an example, which 'say' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Springbok is the nickname for a South African international player, here a touring cricketer.

clue.text: Bumped off, twisting sideways

explanation.surface: Someone was knocked aside and spun around.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the past tense of slay; the other is to swing or skid round.
explanation.definitionFit: Killed is the past tense of slay; to veer or skid round is the other sense.

clue.text: Russian operatic hero provides diversion

parts.note: red is old slang for a Soviet Russian
Albert Herring is the hero of Britten's comic opera

explanation.surface: A Russian tenor creates a distraction on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A misleading clue that distracts attention is a false trail.

clue.text: Steal sovereign or pound

parts.note: to nick is to steal
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the sovereign

explanation.surface: A thief may take a gold coin or a pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' looks like the coin but means the monarch, ER. Nicker is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicker is British slang for one pound sterling, like quid.

clue.text: Female who fought on copper's side once

definitions.text: Female who fought on copper's side once

parts.words: Female who fought on copper's side once
parts.note: an armed woman with shield and trident appeared on the back of the old British penny

explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; it is a copper coin, the pre-decimal penny, which showed this helmeted figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmeted female figure of the nation appeared on old British pennies.

clue.text: Criticize a batsman's effort

explanation.surface: Run down a batter's innings.
explanation.walkthrough: A batsman's innings in cricket is informally called this.
explanation.definitionFit: To find fault is one sense; a cricket innings is the other.

clue.text: On a river bank, the principal water-plant

parts.note: taken as written
a bank is a row, as in a bank of switches
the head is the principal, as of a school

explanation.surface: A head teacher sits on a riverbank beside a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' looks like a riverside, but it means a row or tier.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrowhead is a pond plant named for its arrow-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Foreign capital in company affected by inflation?

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is affected by being filled, so the inflating gas goes inside it

parts.note: inflation is done with air, as of a tyre or balloon

explanation.surface: A firm abroad is hit by rising prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inflation' suggests rising prices, but here it means blowing up a balloon or tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt, a city abroad to a British solver.

clue.text: Waste away without a first prize

indicators.note: without says the letter a is dropped from the word for wasting away

parts.note: to atrophy is to waste away

explanation.surface: Someone loses strength because they never won the top award.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or shield awarded to the winner is the usual first prize.

clue.text: Skier's turn left inside first of two targets

indicators.note: inside first of says the left letter goes into the first of the two target words

parts.note: a tee is a target in curling or quoits
a mark is a target to aim at

explanation.surface: A skier swerves left between two marker targets.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase, 'two targets', supplies both target words; 'inside first of' sends the L into the first one only.
explanation.definitionFit: The telemark is a ski turn with one knee bent and the other ski advanced.

clue.text: Signal to start fighting slightly mistimed

explanation.surface: The bell goes a fraction late.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxing's call clears the corner helpers before a round; read literally it means off by a few seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing referee's call clears trainers from the ring; also, off by a matter of moments.

clue.text: Best way three Rs can produce fruitful result

indicators.note: can produce says these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: three Rs means three letters R

explanation.surface: Advice that the best way to succeed is reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three Rs' suggests the basics of education, reading, writing and arithmetic; here it is just three letters for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A berry is the result of a fruiting plant, so the strawberry is a playful fruit-bearing outcome.

clue.text: Sensible part of procedure, a list I compiled

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clerk claims a checklist he drew up is a sensible part of the process.
explanation.definitionFit: Practical and down-to-earth judgement is sensible.

clue.text: Ken sounds negative

indicators.note: sounds says the word for negative is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: no is a negative answer

explanation.surface: A man called Ken seems to be saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is not a name but the verb meaning to know, a Scottish usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ken is a Scots verb for to be aware of or to understand.

clue.text: Watch over meadow? Primrose survived there

parts.note: a wake is a watch kept over a body
a field is a meadow

explanation.surface: A gardener keeps watch on a field where a primrose lived on.
explanation.walkthrough: Primrose is not a flower but Dr Primrose, Goldsmith's Vicar of Wakefield, who survives many misfortunes there.
explanation.definitionFit: The novel's vicar, Dr Primrose, lives through his troubles in that Yorkshire town.

clue.text: Exclamation from Pat, on finding punch among drinks

indicators.note: among says the punch word goes inside the drinks word

parts.note: beers are drinks
a jab is a punch

explanation.surface: An Irishman cries out when someone throws a punch in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat is a stock name for an Irishman, and this is a mock-Irish oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic Irish oath, a softened form of by Jesus.

clue.text: Expensive letter-opener

explanation.surface: A pricey device for slitting envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter-opener' suggests a paper knife; it is the word that begins a letter, as in Dear Sir.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly is one sense; the other is the salutation at the start of correspondence.

clue.text: Possibly a Monet? Bunk — it's a fake

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An art critic dismisses a supposed Monet as bunk and a forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges A MONET BUNK.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack or charlatan is a fraud, a fake person.

clue.text: Second best, making a frightful noise

parts.note: the cream is the best part

explanation.surface: Coming second when you wanted to be best makes you yell.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek of terror is a loud cry of fright.

clue.text: Make up team as announced for match

indicators.note: as announced says the words are heard spoken, not written

parts.note: to coin is to make up, as a phrase, and a side is a team

explanation.surface: A manager names his team for the coming game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up' is coin, as in coin a word, and 'team' is side; spoken together they give a verb meaning correspond.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that agree or correspond exactly can be said to tally.

clue.text: Plants leader of claque before start of play

indicators.note: before says the first letter goes ahead of the opening-act letters
leader of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: Act I is the start of a play

explanation.surface: The head of the hired applause team plants himself before the curtain rises.
explanation.walkthrough: A claque is a group hired to applaud in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiny desert succulents are a family of plants.

clue.text: Service provided in Peak District

parts.note: Mass is a church service
if means provided, as a condition

explanation.surface: A church service held somewhere in Derbyshire's national park.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peak District is an English national park; here the phrase means a mountainous area.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact group of mountains forms a single upland region.

clue.text: Lacking sparkle, nevertheless

explanation.surface: Flat, all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Lacking sparkle is still water as opposed to fizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat, non-fizzy water is one sense; however is the other.

clue.text: Reportedly tolerates this stream of hate

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: sticks means tolerates, as in can't stick it

explanation.surface: Rumour says this river of loathing is endured.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Styx is the underworld river whose name means hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek underworld river's name comes from the word for loathing.

clue.text: Dish that is divided initially

indicators.note: initially says the divided word comes first, before the that-is letters

parts.note: cut means divided
IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A dish that has been split up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' is slang for an attractive person, not a plate of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish is slang for an attractive person, as is a sweetie or looker.

clue.text: Picked extra

explanation.surface: A selected bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: Picked for the team means included in the side; extra means as an additional item or sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is chosen for the team; the other is as a supplement or sideline.

clue.text: Money-earner's capital taken in awful exaction

definitions.text: Money-earner's capital taken in awful exaction

indicators.note: taken in says the capital letter goes inside the rearranged letters
awful says the letters are messed up into a new order
capital means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A complaint that the state grabs a wage-earner's wealth in a dreadful levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges EXACTION; 'capital' gives M, the first letter of Money-earner's, which 'taken in' puts inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the levy on wages that the state collects from earners.

clue.text: Vegetarian dish for young 4 ac

parts.note: a young antelope from the earlier answer grazes, so its meal is greens

explanation.walkthrough: 4 across is an antelope as well as a cricketer; a grazing calf eats leaves, and 'salad days' also means youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafy raw vegetables are the meal a plant-eating young animal would have.
